stories.h: Pregnancy termination plea: Supreme Court rejects woman's request to abort

paras.t: On Wednesday, the Supreme Court of India refused to allow a woman's plea for medical termination of her pregnancy.
On 26 October, the Bombay High Court dismissed the woman's plea.
On Wednesday 4 November 2026, the Supreme Court rejected a woman's petition seeking permission to medically abort a pregnancy of more than 6 months.
They dismissed a married woman's plea to terminate her nearly 26-week pregnancy.
The bench of Justice BV Nagarathna and Justice R Mahadevan heard the case.
The woman cited marital discord with her husband as the reason for the termination plea.

The woman cited an ongoing marital dispute with her husband as the reason for her request, and alleged mental harassment and humiliation by the husband, including the circulation of a video questioning her character.
The woman's husband opposed the abortion, stating that the husband also has rights over the unborn child.
The case is different from cases involving rape, sexual harassment, or fetal abnormalities, the bench said.

stories.h: Mercedes-Benz electric SUV sold out until March 2027 after 1,000 bookings

paras.t: On Wednesday 4 November 2026, Mercedes-Benz launched the Mercedes GLC Electric SUV in the Indian market.
The Mercedes GLC Electric SUV was sold out until March 2027.
It is larger than the petrol-diesel GLC SUV.
It received a strong response before launch.
The available colors are Sheer Blue, Lavender Silver, Obsidian Black, Opalite White Bright, Patagonia Red Metallic, and Alpine Grey Solid.
Interior color options include black, beach brown, and ivory beige.
The car features an AMG styling package as standard and an all-wheel drive system.
The car body has a clean and smooth design.
The rear of the electric SUV features a gloss-black panel containing the taillamps and the Mercedes logo.

stories.h: Top court overturns 2003 precedent on two-child limit for local government candidates

paras.t: In July 2003, the Supreme Court upheld the provision of the Haryana Panchayati Raj Act, 1994, which disqualified individuals from contesting Panchayat elections for having more than two living children.
On Wednesday, the Supreme Court held that laws penalising having more than two children have lost their relevance due to falling fertility rate.

The bench recommended referring the 2003 Javed v. State of Haryana case to a larger bench while making observations on laws restricting individuals with more than two children from contesting local body elections.
The Supreme Court granted relief to Mangla Bhimrao Ingle, a former sarpanch of Kakoda Gram Panchayat in Maharashtra, in this matter.

The bench of Justice P S Narasimha and Justice Alok Aradhe set aside the disqualification of Mangla Bhimrao, former sarpanch of Kakoda Gram Panchayat, imposed under Section 14(1)(j-1) of the Maharashtra Village Panchayats Act 1959 due to the birth of her third child.
Mangala Bhimrao Ingle's election as sarpanch of Maharashtra's Kakoda gram panchayat was set aside because she had more than two children.

stories.h: Delhi-NCR pollution: Commission for Air Quality Management bans outdoor construction activities

paras.t: On 2 November, the Commission for Air Quality Management ordered restrictions on dust-generating construction and demolition activities across Delhi-NCR.
On Monday, the Municipal Corporation of Gurugram announced a 15-day suspension of outdoor construction and demolition work.
The Commission for Air Quality Management issued instructions to implement all necessary steps under GRAP Stage-II effective from 2 November 2026.
The Air Quality Index in Delhi-NCR was 334 on Tuesday morning.
Parking fees were being increased to discourage the use of private vehicles.
Air pollution levels in Gurugram continued to rise, leading to the ban and office restrictions.
On 4 November 2026, the administration took strict steps to stop pollution in Delhi-NCR.
Exempted projects must continue to follow dust mitigation measures and comply with the Construction and Demolition Waste Management Rules.
Dust-generating demolition and outdoor construction activities would remain restricted across NCR, with exemptions for essential and national importance projects.

stories.h: Supreme Court weighs if police facial recognition at protests violates privacy

paras.t: On November Chief Justice of India Surya Kant, Justice Joymalya Bagchi raised the question of what constitutes a reasonable expectation of privacy when a person is present in a public place.
On Sunday 11 October 2026, the Supreme Court of India issued a notice to the Centre regarding the Cockroach Janta Party protest.
Tushar Mehta said.
On Tuesday, the Supreme Court agreed to examine the contours of the right to privacy of people when they are part of a public protest.
They said they would consider if surveillance by Delhi Police during July protests at Jantar Mantar amounts to negative State interference.
Advocate Prashant Bhushan sought clarifications on the security of the data collected.

A bench comprising Chief Justice of India Surya KantBagchi and Justice V Mohana heard a petition filed by the Software Freedom Law Centre, and it sought the Centre's response on a similar petition filed by Rajya Sabha MP AA Rahim.
Bagchi termed the argument very simplistic and distinguished between the mere association of a face with an individual and the subsequent utilization of collected surveillance data.
Bagchi observed that the amendment to the Identification of Prisoners Act enabled the State to utilize iris identification for crime detection.

stories.h: CEC immunity challenge: Supreme Court seeks response from Centre and poll body

paras.t: On Wednesday, the Supreme Court sought a response from the Centre and the Election Commission over a plea challenging immunity to Chief Election Commissioner and other Election Commissioners from legal action.
The Supreme Court raised several sharp and direct questions on the functioning of the Election Commission to protect the democratic and constitutional rights of voters.
The Supreme Court bench asked the Election Commission if the Special Intensive Revision process was intended to harass or torture voters.

Petitions were filed by RJD MP Manoj Jha (represented by Tanya Srivastava and advocate Arun Kumar Agarwal, represented by advocate Neha Rathi) challenging Section 16 of The Chief Election Commissioner And Other Election Commissioners (Appointment, Conditions Of Service And Term Of Office) Act, 2023.
The Supreme Court bench of Chief Justice Suryakant, Justice Joymalya Bagchi, and Justice V Mohana sought a response on the public interest litigation.

On Wednesday, 4 November 2026, the Supreme Court sought a response from the Union government on petitions challenging the constitutionality of a specific provision in the Chief Election Commissioner-Election Commissioners' appointment law.
A Bench headed by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant issued notice to the Centre and the Election Commission of India on petitions filed by Jha and advocate Agarwal.
On Wednesday 4 November 2026, the Supreme Court bench of Bagchi, and Justice V Mohana issued a notice.
The court told the commission set the next date of hearing as 19 November

stories.h: Agniveer policy update: Cabinet approves two-year extension for 75% of recruits

paras.t: On 3 November, the Central Cabinet decided that 25% of Agniveers would become regular soldiers, while 75 percent of Agniveers would be given a two-year service extension.
The scheme was introduced on 14 June 2022, Chief of Defence Staff N S Raja Subramani said.
The government took this step at a time when the tenure of nearly 18,000 Agniveers in the armed forces was about to be completed.
The four years of the first batch of Agniveers are about to complete.
Yesterday, the government decided to grant an additional two-year tenure to 75% of Agniveers after their four-year service.
Before Diwali, the central government made a major announcement regarding the service extension scheme.
The Cabinet's decision has opened the path for all Agniveers to join the armed forces.
Before Subramani announced the decision to extend the service tenure of 75 percent of Agniveers by two years.

After completing the additional two years, eligible Agniveers who meet selection criteria would have the opportunity to join the regular Armed Forces, and it would allow Agniveers to get the opportunity to serve for six years instead of the stipulated four-year tenure.

stories.h: Seventy per cent of India crude oil imports remain dependent on Hormuz

paras.t: Amir Hayat-Moghaddam stated in an interview with the Iranian Students’ News Agency, "We have currently exempted India, China, Iraq and Qatar from transit restrictions in the Strait of Hormuz. Ships from these countries pass freely, and the Americans do not intercept them either."
Iran decided to close the Strait of Hormuz and impose restrictions on the passage of merchant shipping.
Continuing restrictions on shipping exist in it.

On Wednesday 4 November 2026, Iran announced exemptions for India, China, Iraq, and Qatar from restrictions imposed on ships passing through Hormuz, and it exempted merchant vessels from these countries from restrictions on using the Strait of Hormuz, while it also repeated that Bharatiya ships are exempted.

and it exempted merchant vessels from these countries from restrictions on using the Strait of Hormuz,
while it also repeated that Bharatiya ships are exempted.

paras.t: India has repeatedly called for the unimpeded movement of energy supplies and freedom of navigation in international waterways.
It serves as a necessary energy lifeline for the country.
Iranian Parliament National Security and Foreign Policy Committee Vice Chairman Ahamed Hayat-Moghaddam spoke at a meeting held to review economic and security conditions.
Iran is collecting transit fees from Indian and Chinese ships.
Amir Hayat-Moghaddam did not specify whether Iraqi vessels have to pay transit fees.

stories.h: Cabinet funds 850 fast-track courts to try rape and child abuse cases

paras.t: The Union Cabinet approved the continuation of a central scheme to strengthen fast track special courts to deal with child abuse and rape cases and increase their number from 779 to 850.
Union minister Ashwini Vaishnaw briefed reporters on the decisions taken by the Cabinet.
Chief of Defence Staff General Subramani briefed reporters on a decision concerning Agniveers.
The Central Cabinet approved the expansion and strengthening of 850 fast-track courts.
On Wednesday, 4 November, the Union Cabinet approved 850 fast-track courts for rape and child abuse cases.
Vaishnaw announced that they will be set up for cases of child sexual abuse and rape.
They seek to ensure time-bound trials in pending rape, sexual assault and child abuse cases.
The Centrally Sponsored Scheme for setting up Fast Track Special Courts (FTSCs), including exclusive Pocso courts, was introduced in October 2019.
With Wednesday's approval, it aims to strengthen and extend the network of 850 fast-track courts to expedite the judicial process in cases involving sexual assault and rape of children.
